prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, full body dual-body portrait: real skin down to her collarbones only, never reaching her chest, with a plain water-filled glass body below that exact line. ONE woman standing, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, camera set back so her whole body fits in frame, face still sharp. Mid 20s.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult French woman in French red-lip makeup — fair natural skin with a light dewy finish, softly brushed natural brows, a barely-there brown liner and fluttering lashes, no eyeshadow, soft natural colour on the cheeks, large eyes with bright real catchlights, a single bold classic red lip with a soft matte finish, long dark-brown hair in an effortless tousled updo, an unbothered, effortless expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. A single thick gold hoop hangs on each ear.

Physique: A towering top-heavy hourglass woman standing tall on long legs, never short or squat. A colossal chest far wider than her shoulders curving forward as one enormous rounded mass, a waist that pulls in sharply below it, enormous round hips flaring out to more than twice the width of her shoulders, her entire left leg, foot and glass sandal are part of the vessel above, all the way to the base of each toe; her entire right leg, foot and glass sandal are part of the vessel above, all the way to the base of each toe.

Boundary (skin to material, strictly at the collarbones): a single straight, flat line runs around the base of her neck and across both collarbones, nowhere lower, never reaching her chest — never jagged, never zigzag, a clean straight cut like a cross-section, exactly like a clean slice through a cast-glass sculpture. Real skin above this straight line, the glass vessel immediately below it. At that line, the full thickness of the glass wall is visible edge-on; the glass's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow. The vessel is already full of water right up to this same straight collarbone line and no higher.

Material body: below the collarbones — her whole chest, both arms, both hands, belly, hips, and her entire left leg, foot and glass sandal are part of the vessel above, all the way to the base of each toe, and her entire right leg, foot and glass sandal are part of the vessel above, all the way to the base of each toe — is a sculpted vessel of thick, crystal-clear glass, completely filled with plain clear citrine-gold water, no hollow space anywhere, no fish, no plants, nothing floating — just clear water.

Left leg transition: Her left foot, including its toes, is almost entirely made of the same glass vessel and clear water as the rest of that leg, standing in an extreme platform stiletto sandal carved from that same glass. Only the last few millimetres at the very tip of each toe on the left foot are different — no wider than the toenail itself — where the real toenail and the tiny pad of real flesh just behind it are genuinely real, living flesh. Everything else on that foot — the rest of each toe, the whole foot, and the sandal — is entirely glass. This tiny real tip on each toe is a separate thing entirely from the glass around it, sharing nothing with it — an ordinary, undisturbed real toe-tip, never itself cut, never marked. The glass foot and sandal end cleanly and deliberately right at the base of each of these real toe-tips.

Right leg transition: Her right foot, including its toes, is almost entirely made of the same glass vessel and clear water as the rest of that leg, standing in an extreme platform stiletto sandal carved from that same glass. Only the last few millimetres at the very tip of each toe on the right foot are different — no wider than the toenail itself — where the real toenail and the tiny pad of real flesh just behind it are genuinely real, living flesh. Everything else on that foot — the rest of each toe, the whole foot, and the sandal — is entirely glass. This tiny real tip on each toe is a separate thing entirely from the glass around it, sharing nothing with it — an ordinary, undisturbed real toe-tip, never itself cut, never marked. The glass foot and sandal end cleanly and deliberately right at the base of each of these real toe-tips.

Left leg (real): only the tiny real toe-tips on her left foot, natural skin texture. her left foot stands in a matching glass sandal, carved from the same clear material.

Right leg (real): only the tiny real toe-tips on her right foot, natural skin texture. her right foot stands in a matching glass sandal, carved from the same clear material.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a warm golden amber on one side and a bright citrus yellow on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle — glowing evenly, marked with a few thin dark vertical lines spaced evenly across it so the bending of those lines inside her material body is unmistakable, and a glossy dark floor beneath her feet.

Pose: standing tall, angled 45 degrees, left hand (glass) on her hip, right arm (glass) held clear of her body, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: the glowing backdrop floods her material body from behind, so amber light passes through one side and yellow light passes through the other, the vertical lines clearly visible bending inside the glass. A soft frontal light falls on her face, ears and any real leg parts. A thin cool rim light traces her whole figure. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
